steps.thought: I will list the available tests on the test station to inspect the subsystems of the drone.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: Run power_on_selftest to quickly check all major buses and devices (I2C, UART, CAN) for initial faults at a low cost.
steps.observation: The power_on_selftest passed boot, I2C, UART, and CAN checks, but failed on the camera sensor ID read. This points towards a potential camera sensor dead or ribbon cable fault.

hypotheses.rationale: Camera sensor ID read failed during power-on selftest, indicating the sensor itself may be dead or unresponsive.
Camera sensor ID read failure could also be caused by a loose or damaged CSI ribbon cable preventing communication.

steps.thought: I need to run the camera selftest to determine if the camera sensor is completely dead or if it's a communication issue related to the CSI ribbon cable.
steps.observation: The camera selftest confirms sensor ID not readable and 0.0 fps, confirming a critical camera hardware failure. This rules out software mismatches and narrows the issue down to a dead sensor or a ribbon cable fault.

hypotheses.rationale: Complete inability to read sensor ID and zero frame rate strongly suggests a dead or non-functional camera sensor module.
A damaged or disconnected CSI ribbon cable could also explain the failure to read sensor ID and communicate with the camera.

steps.thought: Camera selftest and power_on_selftest both confirm sensor ID is unreadable and frame rate is 0 fps, indicating a dead camera sensor module.
